A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenWorldSAM and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite pagination changes and relocation of the checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, RefCOCOg fine-tuning results, component ablations, and outdoor generalization analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds query-count and attention-depth ablations plus inference timing measurements in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The frozen SAM2/BEiT-3 architecture, projector, positional tie-breakers, three-layer soft prompting, training objective, and optional two-stage refinement remain unchanged. The new query-count and attention-depth variants test the existing method through ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO training, RefCOCOg evaluation, ADE20K/PASCAL/ScanNet/SUN-RGBD benchmarks, and Cityscapes/BDD10K analyses. The new ablations reuse existing benchmarks; discussion of crowded scenes and alternative encoders does not introduce new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ESC-Net, and Table 3 adds Sa2VA with InternVL2-1B and InternVL2-4B foundations. Existing comparators, including the controlled X-Decoder oracle-prompt comparison in Table 2, remain.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 changes the stated RefCOCOg fine-tuning budget from 15 to 10 epochs, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Appendix F adds query-count and attention-depth settings and AR@100 reporting. Appendix G introduces timing tests for one versus six prompts on a 1024×1024 image using an A5000 GPU.

E4.justification: Appendix F substantially extends the existing component ablations by testing K=10/20/30 and comparing zero, one, and three attention layers across retained benchmarks. Appendix G adds module-level runtime profiling and prompt-count scaling analysis. Existing refinement examples and outdoor robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G newly reports averaging inference timings over five independent runs. The checklist's fixed-seed explanation and absence of error bars remain unchanged; no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run variability are added for segmentation accuracy.

E6.justification: Earlier segmentation accuracy values are retained, but substantial sensitivity and timing results are added. Table 11 reports AP 14.2/16.9/16.5 for K=10/20/30, and Table 12 adds one-layer and expanded no-attention results. Tables 13–14 report 460.69/688.50 ms for one/six prompts. New comparator entries include ESC-Net's 41.8 ADE-150 mIoU and Sa2VA's 72.3/74.1 RefCOCOg cIoU.

T1.justification: The query construction equation and mathematical method descriptions are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the added query-count and runtime discussion is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified language-prompted segmentation, multi-instance tie-breakers, lightweight frozen-backbone adaptation, and strong zero-shot/referring performance. Removing the abstract's benchmark-name list does not change the claims' scope.

C2.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B qualify refinement benefits as applying to correctly localized predictions and explain how refinement can amplify localization errors. Appendices F–G add interpretations of query saturation, the one-layer accuracy/parameter tradeoff, and amortized inference costs. Existing outdoor limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct project-code link and documents the new profiling setup. Table 5 revises E2/E3 parameter counts from 1.7M to 1.3M, while Table 9 revises several SAM ViT-H backbone counts from 2.4B to 636M. These are reporting revisions; new Table 12 inconsistently retains 1.7M for the no-attention variant.

R1.justification: Four references are added concerning ESC-Net, Sa2VA, InternVL2, and expected object-detection queries. They support the added comparisons and query-count discussion. The earlier 75 cited works and Section 2's research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, adds acknowledgements and Appendices F–G, and updates the conference footer. The checklist moves from after the appendices to immediately after the references. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 gain comparator rows, and Tables 11–14 introduce compact ablation and timing displays. There are limited caption, table-formatting, and page-flow adjustments. Figures 1–9 and the existing visual organization are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity experiments and measured timing breakdowns better support the existing design and efficiency claims. Added comparators and explanations of refinement failures also improve scrutiny. These benefits outweigh limited reporting problems, particularly the conflicting parameter counts in Tables 5 and 12 and the unexplained fine-tuning budget revision accompanying an unchanged RefCOCOg score.
